verses.original: δὲ Σαῦλος ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ αὐτοῦ ἀναιρέσει δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μέγας διωγμὸς Ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις δὲ πάντες πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας
verses.transliteration: de Saulos ēn syneudokōn tē autou anairesei de en ekeinē tē hēmera megas diōgmos Egeneto epi tēn ekklēsian tēn en Hierosolymois de pantes plēn tōn apostolōn diesparēsan kata tas chōras tēs Ioudaias kai Samareias
verses.literal: And Saul was there giving approval to [Stephen’s] death - On that - day a great persecution broke out against the church - in Jerusalem and all except the apostles were scattered throughout . . . . . . - Judea and Samaria

verses.original: δὲ εὐλαβεῖς ἄνδρες συνεκόμισαν τὸν Στέφανον καὶ ἐποίησαν μέγαν κοπετὸν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: de eulabeis andres synekomisan ton Stephanon kai epoiēsan megan kopeton ep’ autō
verses.literal: - God-fearing men buried - Stephen and vvv vvv mourned deeply over him

verses.original: δὲ Σαῦλος ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν εἰσπορευόμενος κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους τε σύρων ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν
verses.transliteration: de Saulos elymaineto tēn ekklēsian eisporeuomenos kata tous oikous te syrōn andras kai gynaikas paredidou eis phylakēn
verses.literal: But Saul began to destroy the church Going from house to house . . . . . . - he dragged off men and women [and] put [them] in prison

verses.original: οὖν μὲν Οἱ διασπαρέντες εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον διῆλθον
verses.transliteration: oun men Hoi diasparentes euangelizomenoi ton logon diēlthon
verses.literal: - - Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went

verses.original: δὲ Φίλιππος κατελθὼν εἰς τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Χριστόν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: de Philippos katelthōn eis tēn polin tēs Samareias ekēryssen ton Christon autois
verses.literal: - Philip went down to - [a] city - [in] Samaria [and] proclaimed the Christ to them

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι ὁμοθυμαδὸν προσεῖχον τοῖς ἐν τῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου λεγομένοις ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ τὰ σημεῖα βλέπειν ἃ ἐποίει
verses.transliteration: de hoi ochloi homothymadon proseichon tois en tō hypo tou Philippou legomenois akouein autous kai ta sēmeia blepein ha epoiei
verses.literal: - The crowds all paid close attention - vvv . . . vvv vvv to Philip’s message . . . . . . and to the signs they saw - him perform

verses.original: γὰρ βοῶντα μεγάλῃ φωνῇ ἀκάθαρτα πνεύματα ἐξήρχοντο πολλοὶ τῶν ἐχόντων δὲ πολλοὶ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν
verses.transliteration: gar boōnta megalē phōnē akatharta pneumata exērchonto polloi tōn echontōn de polloi paralelymenoi kai chōloi etherapeuthēsan
verses.literal: - vvv vvv With loud shrieks unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed and many [of the] paralyzed and lame were healed

verses.original: δὲ ἐγένετο πολλὴ χαρὰ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ πόλει
verses.transliteration: de egeneto pollē chara en ekeinē tē polei
verses.literal: So there was great joy in that - city

verses.original: δέ προϋπῆρχεν τις Ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Σίμων μαγεύων ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας λέγων ἑαυτὸν εἶναί τινα μέγαν
verses.transliteration: de proupērchen tis Anēr onomati Simōn mageuōn en tē polei kai existanōn to ethnos tēs Samareias legōn heauton einai tina megan
verses.literal: - Prior to that time a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people - of Samaria He claimed . . . to be someone great

verses.original: πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου προσεῖχον ᾧ λέγοντες Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ δύναμις ἡ καλουμένη Μεγάλη
verses.transliteration: pantes apo mikrou heōs megalou proseichon hō legontes Houtos estin hē tou Theou dynamis hē kaloumenē Megalē
verses.literal: [and] all [the people] from the least to the greatest heeded [ his words ] . . . [and] said This [man] is the - divine power - called [the] Great [Power]

verses.original: δὲ προσεῖχον αὐτῷ διὰ ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις
verses.transliteration: de proseichon autō dia exestakenai autous to hikanō chronō tais mageiais
verses.literal: - They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with [his] sorcery

verses.original: δὲ Ὅτε ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβαπτίζοντο τε ἄνδρες καὶ γυναῖκες
verses.transliteration: de Hote episteusan tō Philippō euangelizomenō peri tēs basileias tou Theou kai tou onomatos Iēsou Christou ebaptizonto te andres kai gynaikes
verses.literal: But when they believed - Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom - of God and the name of Jesus Christ they were baptized both men and women

verses.original: δὲ καὶ ὁ Σίμων αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ τε ἐξίστατο μεγάλας σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις θεωρῶν γινομένας
verses.transliteration: de kai ho Simōn autos episteusen kai baptistheis ēn proskarterōn tō Philippō te existato megalas sēmeia kai dynameis theōrōn ginomenas
verses.literal: - Even - Simon himself believed and was baptized vvv He followed - Philip {closely} and was astounded [by the] great signs and miracles he observed . . .

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις Ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἡ Σαμάρεια δέδεκται τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπέστειλαν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην πρὸς αὐτοὺς
verses.transliteration: de hoi apostoloi en Hierosolymois Akousantes hoti hē Samareia dedektai ton logon tou Theou apesteilan Petron kai Iōannēn pros autous
verses.literal: [When] the apostles in Jerusalem heard that - Samaria had received the word - of God they sent Peter and John to them

verses.original: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα
verses.transliteration: hoitines katabantes prosēuxanto peri autōn hopōs labōsin Hagion Pneuma
verses.literal: vvv On their arrival they prayed for them to receive [the] Holy Spirit

verses.original: γὰρ ἦν οὐδέπω ἐπιπεπτωκός ἐπ’ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν δὲ ὑπῆρχον μόνον βεβαπτισμένοι εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: gar ēn oudepō epipeptōkos ep’ oudeni autōn de hypērchon monon bebaptismenoi eis to onoma tou kyriou Iēsou
verses.literal: For [the Holy Spirit] had not yet fallen upon any of them - they had simply been . . . baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus

verses.original: τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπ’ αὐτούς καὶ ἐλάμβανον Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα
verses.transliteration: tote epetithesan tas cheiras ep’ autous kai elambanon Hagion Pneuma
verses.literal: Then [Peter and John] laid [their] hands on them and they received [the] Holy Spirit

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Σίμων Ἰδὼν ὅτι τὸ Πνεῦμα δίδοται διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων χειρῶν προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα
verses.transliteration: de ho Simōn Idōn hoti to Pneuma didotai dia tēs epitheseōs tōn tōn apostolōn cheirōn prosēnenken autois chrēmata
verses.literal: [When] - Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the - apostles’ hands he offered them money

verses.original: Δότε ταύτην τὴν ἐξουσίαν κἀμοὶ λέγων ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ Ἅγιον Πνεῦμα
verses.transliteration: Dote tautēn tēn exousian kamoi legōn hina hō ean epithō tas cheiras lambanē Hagion Pneuma
verses.literal: Give {me} this - power as well he said so that everyone on whom . . . I lay [my] hands may receive [the] Holy Spirit

verses.original: δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν σου Τὸ ἀργύριόν εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν σὺν σοὶ ὅτι ἐνόμισας κτᾶσθαι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ χρημάτων
verses.transliteration: de Petros eipen pros auton sou To argyrion eiē eis apōleian syn soi hoti enomisas ktasthai tēn dōrean tou Theou dia chrēmatōn
verses.literal: But Peter replied - - {May} your - silver perish . . . . . . with you because you thought you could buy the gift - of God with money

verses.original: σοι ἔστιν οὐκ μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ γὰρ σου ἡ καρδία ἔστιν οὐκ εὐθεῖα ἔναντι τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: soi estin ouk meris oude klēros en toutō tō logō gar sou hē kardia estin ouk eutheia enanti tou Theou
verses.literal: You have no part [or] share in - [our] ministry because your - heart is not right before - God

verses.original: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς σου κακίας καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ Κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς σου καρδίας
verses.transliteration: metanoēson oun apo tautēs tēs sou kakias kai deēthēti tou Kyriou ei ara aphethēsetai soi hē epinoia tēs sou kardias
verses.literal: Repent therefore of - - your wickedness and pray to the Lord vvv Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart

verses.original: γὰρ ὁρῶ σε ὄντα εἰς χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας
verses.transliteration: gar horō se onta eis cholēn pikrias kai syndesmon adikias
verses.literal: For I see that you are - poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Σίμων Ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ὑμεῖς Δεήθητε πρὸς τὸν Κύριον ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ὅπως μηδὲν ὧν εἰρήκατε ἐπέλθῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ
verses.transliteration: de ho Simōn Apokritheis eipen hymeis Deēthēte pros ton Kyrion hyper emou hopōs mēden hōn eirēkate epelthē ep’ eme
verses.literal: Then - Simon answered . . . - Pray to the Lord for me so that nothing - you have said may happen to me

verses.original: οὖν μὲν Οἱ διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπέστρεφον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα τε εὐηγγελίζοντο πολλάς τῶν Σαμαριτῶν κώμας
verses.transliteration: oun men Hoi diamartyramenoi kai lalēsantes ton logon tou Kyriou hypestrephon eis Hierosolyma te euēngelizonto pollas tōn Samaritōn kōmas
verses.literal: And after - [Peter and John] had testified and spoken the word of the Lord they returned to Jerusalem - preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages

verses.original: δὲ Ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν
verses.transliteration: de Angelos Kyriou elalēsen pros Philippon legōn Anastēthi kai poreuou kata mesēmbrian epi tēn hautē estin erēmos hodon tēn katabainousan apo Ierousalēm eis Gazan
verses.literal: Now an angel of [the] Lord said to Philip - Get up and go - south to the - - desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς καὶ ἐπορεύθη ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης αὐτῆς τῆς γάζης Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων ὃς ἐληλύθει εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ προσκυνήσων
verses.transliteration: kai anastas kai eporeuthē idou anēr Aithiops eunouchos dynastēs hos ēn epi pasēs autēs tēs gazēs Kandakēs basilissēs Aithiopōn hos elēlythei eis Ierousalēm proskynēsōn
verses.literal: [So] he started out and on his way [he met] vvv an Ethiopian eunuch a court official - - in charge of the entire - - treasury of Candace queen of [the] Ethiopians [He] had gone to Jerusalem to worship

verses.original: τε ὑποστρέφων ἦν καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ ἅρματος καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην
verses.transliteration: te hypostrephōn ēn kai kathēmenos epi autou tou harmatos kai aneginōsken Ēsaian ton prophētēn
verses.literal: and on his return was - sitting in his - chariot - reading Isaiah the prophet

verses.original: δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα Εἶπεν τῷ Φιλίππῳ Πρόσελθε τούτῳ τῷ ἅρματι καὶ κολλήθητι
verses.transliteration: de to Pneuma Eipen tō Philippō Proselthe toutō tō harmati kai kollēthēti
verses.literal: - The Spirit said - to Philip Go over to [that] - chariot and stay by [it]

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος Προσδραμὼν ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις καὶ εἶπεν
verses.transliteration: de ho Philippos Prosdramōn ēkousen autou anaginōskontos Ēsaian ton prophētēn Ara ge ginōskeis ha anaginōskeis kai eipen
verses.literal: [So] - Philip ran up [and] heard [the man] reading Isaiah the prophet - - Do you understand what you are reading - [Philip] asked

verses.original: Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην δὲ Ὁ εἶπεν ἐὰν μή τις ὁδηγήσει με τε παρεκάλεσέν τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Pōs gar an dynaimēn de Ho eipen ean mē tis hodēgēsei me te parekalesen ton Philippon anabanta kathisai syn autō
verses.literal: How - vvv can I - - he said unless . . . someone guides me And he invited - Philip to come up [and] sit with him

verses.original: δὲ ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη Ἡ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἤχθη Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα
verses.transliteration: de aneginōsken ēn hautē Hē periochē tēs graphēs hēn ēchthē Hōs probaton epi sphagēn kai hōs amnos enantion tou keirantos auton aphōnos houtōs ouk anoigei autou to stoma
verses.literal: - [The eunuch] was reading . . . this - passage of Scripture - He was led like a sheep to [the] slaughter and as a lamb before the shearer . . . [is] silent so vvv He did not open His - mouth

verses.original: Ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ταπεινώσει ἡ αὐτοῦ ἤρθη κρίσις τίς διηγήσεται αὐτοῦ τὴν γενεὰν ὅτι αὐτοῦ ἡ ζωὴ αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς
verses.transliteration: En tē autou tapeinōsei hē autou ērthē krisis tis diēgēsetai autou tēn genean hoti autou hē zōē airetai apo tēs gēs
verses.literal: In - His humiliation - He was deprived of justice Who can recount His - descendants For His - life was removed from the earth

verses.original: Δέομαί σου δὲ Ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ Φιλίππῳ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει τοῦτο περὶ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ τινός ἑτέρου
verses.transliteration: Deomai sou de Apokritheis eipen tō Philippō ho eunouchos tinos ho prophētēs legei touto peri peri heautou ē peri tinos heterou
verses.literal: Tell me . . . - - said - - the eunuch who {is} the prophet talking . . . about - himself or - someone else

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος Ἀνοίξας ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς γραφῆς καὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: de ho Philippos Anoixas arxamenos apo tautēs tēs graphēs kai autou to stoma euēngelisato autō ton Iēsoun
verses.literal: Then - Philip vvv began with this very - Scripture and - - - told him the good news about . . . - Jesus

verses.original: δὲ Ὡς ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ καί ὁ εὐνοῦχος φησιν Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι
verses.transliteration: de Hōs eporeuonto kata tēn hodon ēlthon epi ti hydōr kai ho eunouchos phēsin Idou hydōr ti kōlyei me baptisthēnai
verses.literal: - As they traveled along the road [and] came to some water - the eunuch said Look [here is] water What is [there] to prevent me [from] being baptized

verses.original: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα καὶ ἀμφότεροι ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος κατέβησαν εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: kai ekeleusen stēnai to harma kai amphoteroi ho te Philippos kai ho eunouchos katebēsan eis to hydōr kai ebaptisen auton
verses.literal: And he gave orders to stop the chariot Then both - - Philip and the eunuch went down into the water and [Philip] baptized him

verses.original: δὲ Ὅτε ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκ οὐκέτι γὰρ ἐπορεύετο αὐτοῦ τὴν ὁδὸν χαίρων
verses.transliteration: de Hote anebēsan ek tou hydatos Pneuma Kyriou hērpasen ton Philippon kai ho eunouchos eiden auton ouk ouketi gar eporeueto autou tēn hodon chairōn
verses.literal: - When they came up out of the water [the] Spirit of [the] Lord carried - Philip {away} and the eunuch saw him vvv no more [but] went on his - way rejoicing

verses.original: δὲ Φίλιππος εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο πάσας τὰς πόλεις ἕως αὐτὸν τοῦ ἐλθεῖν εἰς Καισάρειαν
verses.transliteration: de Philippos heurethē eis Azōton kai dierchomenos euēngelizeto pasas tas poleis heōs auton tou elthein eis Kaisareian
verses.literal: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through [that region] preaching the gospel in all the towns until he - came to Caesarea
